findings.summary: Stale or loose wording: AttnFwd.lean's module docstring puts the test at lines 600-650 and the benchmark at 655-705; testInst is called the test's shape with H = 1; two score estimates.
findings.detail: (1) lean/AttnFwd.lean, module docstring, line 11: "the test (`test_op`, lines 600–650) and the benchmark (lines 655–705)". In source/06-fused-attention.py the test is lines 631–695 and the benchmark lines 698–780 (`bench_flash_attention` 739–775), as README.md says. (2) The docstring of `testInst` ("One head of the test's shape (Z = H = 1, …)") and README.md, Proof ("one head of the test's smallest shape (Z = H = 1, …)"): the test's H is 2 or 48 (line 632), so Z = H = 1 is not a test shape; it is a covered instance, which is all `satisfiable` needs. (3) `HeadOk`'s docstring puts the benchmark's scaled score magnitudes at "about 300 at most", README.md, Specification, at "some 200" at the largest pair; both are far below 2^10 (work/scores.py gives a Chernoff bound of about 240 at D = 128 over the benchmark's 2^35 pairs), but the two texts should agree. Resolve: correct the line numbers, call testInst a covered instance of the test's smallest N_CTX and HEAD_DIM, and give one estimate in both places.

findings.summary: SEMANTICS 'Float + and -' does not say whether the value tl.maximum, tl.minimum or tl.where returns, when it is a product's value, counts as an operand 'computed by *'.
findings.detail: SEMANTICS.md, "Float `+` and `-`: IEEE or fusable": "A product is an operand computed by `*`, `tl.dot` or `tl.rand`, through any dataflow, inlined helpers and library functions included." This kernel's model writes line 84's `m_i - m_ij` as the IEEE `tl.sub` and line 241's `m_i + tl.math.log2(l_i)` as the IEEE `tl.add`, where (STAGE 1 or 3) `m_ij = tl.maximum(m_i, tl.max(qk, 1) * qk_scale)` (line 80), whose value is, on most rows, bit for bit the product `tl.max(qk, 1) * qk_scale`, and the loop carries it into `m_i`. I read the page as: an operand is a product when its defining operation is `*`, `tl.dot` or `tl.rand`, with only bindings, helper returns, loop carries and library helpers in between, so a `tl.maximum` result is not one and the model's IEEE forms are right. But "through any dataflow" can also be read to include operations that pass one of their operands through (`tl.maximum`, `tl.minimum`, `tl.where`, a runtime `if`'s merged value), and then lines 84 and 241 would need `tl.subc` and `tl.addc`. Every online-softmax kernel has this shape. Request: state which operations end a product (or that a `tl.maximum`, `tl.minimum` or `tl.where` result is not one), with evidence if needed. Not blocking: I judged the model under the first reading.

notes: Non-blocking remarks. (a) Tolerances recomputed exactly from the Lean definitions (work/tol.py, work/tol.out): README's table is right; at the host's sizes and inputs tolO is about 0.4% (test, X about 20) and 3% (benchmark, X about 240); at the largest covered case (D = 256, N = 2^16, X = 2^10) tolO = 0.236 and tolM = 0.194, still below 1, so Post fixes each output to within a quarter of the weighted mean of |v|, which I accept since the host's inputs sit four times inside X <= 2^10. The tolS term can reach about 87 absolute when |v| = 2^15 on all 2^16 keys; that is the kernel's own float16 rounding of small p (2^-25 per key), not a weakness of Post. (b) HeadOk bounds the scores over every pair of the head, also above the diagonal of a causal launch, which the kernel never uses; stronger than needed, harmless for real inputs. (c) Model printed with full names (work/print_names.lean, .out): every operation is TVA.* or a kernel helper read in full; axioms propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound.
